summary.headline: Fusion Finance Q2 FY27 net profit rose to INR86 crores and annualised ROA hit about 4%, while AUM growth guidance is being moderated.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 disbursements were INR1,726 crores, up 33% YoY but broadly flat QoQ, and AUM reached INR8,007 crores (+14% YoY) after floods disrupted July and August collections in five states. Gross NPA fell to 1.6% from 2.51% QoQ (2.28% including the INR54 crore ARC sale), and profit after tax reached INR86 crores versus a loss of INR22 crores a year earlier. Cost of borrowing fell for a fifth straight quarter, with marginal cost at 9.35%, and NII margin rose to 12.52%. Management said the INR10,000 crore AUM ambition will likely slip given the H1 disruption, while credit cost and ROA targets are unchanged.

segments.name: Core JLG microfinance
segments.commentary: Remains the majority of the business; average MFI AUM per branch rose to INR5.4 crores from INR5.1 crores, with about 102 branches being rationalised and 50 new branches planned.

segments.name: Premium JLG (income above INR3 lakhs)
segments.commentary: Vishwas product launched in Q2 accounted for about 20% of MFI disbursements in September and October; ticket size capped at INR1 lakh, and loans are reported as MFI JLG under bureau rules.

segments.name: Secured MSME
segments.commentary: About 10% of MSME disbursements now originate through MFI branches, with MFI branches acting as MSME spokes expanded from 50 to 100; MSME disbursements grew about 10% QoQ in October, with MSME ticket size cap raised to INR50 lakhs from INR25 lakhs.

segments.name: Maharashtra (about INR117 crore book)
segments.commentary: Collection efficiency fell to 98.84% in October from 99.4%; net flow rate 0.57%, with the drought-affected sub-book of about INR26-27 crores at about 97.25% collection efficiency.

segments.name: Karnataka (about 1.25% of portfolio)
segments.commentary: Collection efficiency 99.95% in October with negative net flow rate; management reports no stress in the market.

guidance_outlook: AUM ambition of INR10,000 crores is still a medium-term objective, but management said it may moderate and arrive later; no new year-end AUM number given.
Credit cost guided at 2% to 2.5% for the year: about 1.8% base (flows of about 15-16 bps per quarter) plus about 30 bps per quarter if a shock occurs.
Exit-quarter ROA target of 4% has already been achieved (annualised ~4% in Q2); medium-term ROA target is 4%+.
Management expects at least 15-20 bps NIM expansion next quarter and sustained margins thereafter; a further 12-15 bps per quarter of yield uplift is expected over the next two quarters.
Q3 disbursement momentum: October up about 10% over the prior-quarter monthly average (INR568-570 crores), across both MFI and MSME.
Medium-term AUM growth ambition of 20-25% per year, with a calibrated timeline for the INR10,000 crore target.
Management expects a possible 50-75 bps rise in marginal cost of borrowing over the next two quarters, which it says would have a muted impact; rate pass-through is 6-9 months away if needed.
Retention of repeat customers rose to 38-39% from 28-29%; target is 50% over the next few quarters.
capex_capacity: MFI branch network: 950 branches now run on-ground credit assessment, up from about 200 branches.
Branch footprint: about 102 branches being rationalised and 50 new branches planned in markets with strong opportunity.

New LOS and LMS systems live in about 15% of branches, with broader transition targeted before financial year-end; AI capabilities in development for collections, customer service and credit assessment.
Recovery of 90+ DPD legacy portfolio brought in-house; recoveries exceeded INR30 crores in Q2, including INR21 crores from written-off accounts.
demand_pricing: Collection efficiency returned to 99.75% in Q2 with net flow rate below 0.10%; October gross collection efficiency 99.78% (September 99.77%).
Disbursements in October up about 10% over the prior quarter's monthly average of INR568-570 crores, with MFI and MSME each growing about 10%.
Yield rose about 24 bps QoQ from the rate hike taken at the start of FY27; cost of borrowing fell about 35 bps QoQ.
PTC raised INR320 crores at an all-in cost of about 8.5%, now about 10% of borrowings; management aims to raise the PTC share further.
CGSMFI2.0 scheme: accepted about INR468 crores of sanctions at about 9.23% all-in cost out of about INR1,100 crores available; the company declined sanctions with unfavourable terms.
Delinquent receivables on direct assignment fell to 12.65% of AUM from 13.75% QoQ; the company aims to reduce direct assignment reliance.

qa_highlights.question: What were October collection efficiency and disbursement numbers, including for Maharashtra and Karnataka?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross collection efficiency was 99.78% in October (September 99.77%). Maharashtra's INR117 crore book fell to 98.84% (from 99.4%) with a 0.57% net flow rate; Karnataka was at 99.95% with negative net flow.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company accelerate growth in H2 or wait for drought-affected areas to stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has moved almost all of Maharashtra and some bordering Karnataka branches to stricter guardrails with no new customers there, and is pressing growth elsewhere. Maharashtra is about 2% and Karnataka about 1.25% of the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any stress building in districts from rainfall deficit or drought?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no carry-over of stress from September or October into the next month outside Maharashtra. The premium JLG product carries a 0.19% par in the third cycle and above over the past 1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is borrower count falling and what is retention?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 4% of customers hold more than three lenders and will be exited. Repeat-loan retention rose from 28-29% to 38-39% since August, with a target of 50%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 credit cost guidance and how much H1 profit is recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is 2% to 2.5% for the year, with a base of about 1.8% and a further 30 bps per quarter if a shock occurs. Management said INR86.47 crores of profit is recurring with no exceptional items; net credit cost is about 1.2% annualised after recoveries.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins rise, and will rates be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a 15-20 bps margin rise next quarter from yield and PTC-driven borrowing cost benefits, and sees a further 12-15 bps per quarter yield uplift. Any pass-through of rate increases is 6-9 months away and not planned now.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company give a year-end AUM number and a higher exit ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a new year-end AUM figure, citing many moving parts and a likely moderation of the INR10,000 crore target. It said the company enters November with no carry-over of stress and expects growth from individual loans, premium JLG and MSME.

risks_watch: Maharashtra drought: 60% of drought impact not yet seen per management; sub-book at 97.25% collection efficiency, with stricter guardrails and no new customers in the affected areas.
AUM growth: the INR10,000 crore target may slip; growth in the next 4-5 months depends on October's 10% momentum continuing.
Cost of funds: management expects 50-75 bps of rate increase over two quarters, and margin guidance depends on PTC share rising and the CGSMFI2.0 benefit.
Credit cost: 2-2.5% guidance includes a 30 bps per quarter shock allowance; the ARC sale of INR54 crores lifted Stage 3 coverage to 93.4%.
Premium JLG and MSME: higher-ticket products are a new risk; loans above INR3 lakhs income are non-qualified but reported as MFI JLG.
Tax: unrecognised DTA of INR271 crores as of September 30 could be used in future.
summary.management_tone: Confident on credit quality, margins and profitability, with ROA and credit cost targets reiterated. Cautious on growth: management declined to give a new AUM number and said the INR10,000 crore target may be moderated because of the drought and flood disruptions.

rows.label: PTC share rising and CGSMFI2.0 funding benefit
rows.why: PTC raised INR320 crores at about 8.5% (about 10% of borrowings) and management aims to raise the share further; CGSMFI2.0 sanctions of about INR468 crores at 9.23% all-in are a cheaper funding source supporting the margin guide.

rows.label: Delinquent direct-assignment receivables falling

rows.label: Funding pipeline supports growth

tone.note: Management was confident on credit quality (GNPA 1.6%, collection efficiency 99.78% in October), margins and ROA around 4%, but cautious on growth: it declined a year-end AUM number and moderated the INR10,000 crore ambition because of the Maharashtra drought and floods.
